raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Add a fused kernel path for wide-residual hybrid models with shortcut- connected MoE (--wide-residual-shortcut-moe-kernel-fusion). At each shortcut boundary one Gluon kernel mixes the residual streams with the branch updates, writes the new FP32 residual, and emits the RMSNorm readers that consume it (BF16, or an MXFP8 handoff to the next GEMM). The backward pass fuses the matching gradient stages, and checkpointed residuals are reconstructed by forward replay instead of being stored (--residual-stream-recompute-num-layers).

Forward schedules (GB300):
- Training and long prefill: tuned per-shape configs for the production widths and a small decision tree for other shapes (hidden 3072-16384, 1-6 streams), 85-90% of peak DRAM at 4K+ rows.
- Inference: each row's loads are issued before any store, configs come from a decision tree over rows/hidden/streams/readers/precision, and decode rows split across an sm_90+ CTA cluster that exchanges partial sums of squares through distributed shared memory. Launches are programmatic dependents (PDL) on sm_90+.

Residual writes are bit-identical across schedules and match checkpoint replay; reader outputs differ by at most one BF16 ulp between schedules. Adds unit, determinism (CUDA-graph replay), MXFP8, shape and model tests.

- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

+# Fused wide-residual shortcut seams
+
+For wide-residual hybrid models with shortcut-connected MoE (`--moe-shortcut-wide-residual-norm-fusion`;
+needs BF16 parameters, RMSNorm, 2-6 wide streams, a shared expert, no dropout/bias, no CP/PP, no
+layernorm recompute, at most 65536 local tokens per call (16384 above hidden 4096), the fusion
+stack specs, and a GB300 for training — the full list is in the
+`moe_shortcut_wide_residual_norm_fusion` docstring; the residual stream is FP32 with `--fp32-residual-connection`, otherwise BF16, and the
+connection logits may be FP32 or BF16 — all arithmetic is FP32 either way), `ShortcutMoEBlock` replaces
+each residual seam with one Gluon kernel that mixes the wide-residual streams with the branch update,
+writes the new residual, and emits the RMSNorm readers that consume it — directly as MXFP8 for an
+exclusive TE Linear consumer under an MXFP8 recipe, otherwise BF16. `wide_residual_write_read_rmsnorm_quant`
+writes the Mamba/GDN/attention output and produces the shared expert's normalized input; `shortcut_add_wide_residual_write_two_reader_rmsnorm_quant`
+adds the routed and shared MoE outputs (the shortcut add, passed between blocks as a `PendingShortcutAdd`) and
+produces the next block's compute-layer and shortcut-routing inputs. The shortcut add is optional: a
+`PendingShortcutAdd` without a shared update is a single write read twice, which a lone wide-residual
+Mamba or MLP-only layer directly before a fused block uses (M → [* E], - → [* E]) so that block's
+two-reader kernel writes its update and emits both inputs. The matching backward is one fused kernel per seam (plus scratch resets and the final gradient reductions); with
+`--residual-stream-recompute-num-layers N` the residuals are rebuilt by bit-exact checkpoint replay instead
+of being saved. Residual writes are bit-identical to replay and across kernel
+schedules, reader outputs differ by at most one BF16 ulp between schedules, and the tests check every
+output and gradient against independent FP64/autograd references.
+
+| boundary | updates | readers | kernel |
+|---|--:|--:|---|
+| compute → MoE inside a block | 1 | 1 | `wide_residual_write_read_rmsnorm_quant` |
+| lone layer → lone layer (M → -, - → M) | 1 | 1 | `shortcut_add_wide_residual_write_read_rmsnorm_quant`, no shared update |
+| block → lone layer ([* E] → M) | 2 (routed + shared) | 1 | `shortcut_add_wide_residual_write_read_rmsnorm_quant` |
+| block → block (shortcut add) | 2 (routed + shared) | 2 | `shortcut_add_..._two_reader_rmsnorm_quant` |
+| lone layer → block (M → [* E]) | 1 | 2 | `shortcut_add_..._two_reader_rmsnorm_quant`, no shared update |
+
+Lone wide-residual Mamba layers (Mamba or GDP mixers) and MLP-only layers expose the read/RMSNorm
+they apply (`pending_write_reader`) and the write they produce (`pending_write_writer`). When the
+next layer applies a layer's write in its seam kernel, `group_layers_into_shortcut_blocks` sets
+`defers_residual_write` and the layer returns its write as a `PendingShortcutAdd`, which the next
+layer receives as `hidden_states`. In a stack of such layers every seam after the first layer's
+read is one kernel, including under checkpoint replay intervals. MLP-only layers use a standalone
+pre-MLP RMSNorm in the fusion stack specs; lone attention/GDN layers, and lone layers whose calls run
+through a per-layer CUDA graph, are not chained.
+
+The fused seams need the static fusion stack specs (`wide_residual_shortcut_fusion_{,gdp_}{,inference_}stack_spec`
+in `hybrid_layer_specs`), which split every input norm the kernels apply out of its projection; checkpoints
+keep the unsplit keys. Model builders select them with `shortcut_fusion_stack_spec(<wide-residual spec>)`
+(the training builder and `hybrid_builders.py` do so when the flag is set).
+
+## Performance
+
+GB300, Triton 3.7.1, 3 wide streams; fused kernel time per call under CUDA graphs (20 launches per graph
+over rotating input copies with every output kept alive, median of 10 replays). Two modes: an FP32
+residual stream with the MXFP8 handoff of reader zero (reader one, when present, stays BF16), and a BF16
+residual stream (BF16 connection logits) with BF16 readers. %DRAM = compulsory bytes / fused time /
+7.926 TB/s. Forward bytes: residual read + write, BF16 updates, reader outputs and MXFP8 scales, and in
+training the shortcut add's BF16 update sum and rstd. Backward bytes: previous residual, incoming carry and
+residual gradient, saved update, reader and update gradients, rstd, and MXFP8 columns of reader zero
+(materialized in the backward call; with checkpoint replay they come from replay instead). Below 32 tokens
+the forward is the inference kernel (no backward state) and MXFP8 and the backward do not apply (rows must
+be multiples of 32; model training additionally needs multiples of 1024 tokens). The backward time includes
+its scratch resets and final gradient reductions.
+

+"""Model-facing fused shortcut boundaries; GPU imports are lazy.
+
+Training covers the shortcut graph and registered native streamwise consumers,
+including pruned residual/reader gradients, on a qualified GB300.
+No-grad calls bypass autograd and omit all tensors saved for backward.
+"""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from functools import lru_cache
+
+import torch
+from torch.autograd.function import once_differentiable
+
+from .kernel_utils import validate_num_streams
+from .residual_replay import ResidualSlot, current_manager, retained_slot
+
+
+def validate_input(residual, hidden_size, num_streams, *, inference=False):
+    """Validate the local flattened token layout before launching fused work."""
+    validate_num_streams(num_streams)
+    if type(hidden_size) is not int or not 32 <= hidden_size <= 16384 or hidden_size % 32:
+        raise ValueError("shortcut fusion requires H in [32, 16384], divisible by 32")
+    if residual.ndim < 2 or residual.shape[-1] != num_streams * hidden_size:
+        raise ValueError("shortcut fusion expects residual shape [..., S * H]")
+    tokens = residual.numel() // residual.shape[-1]
+    maximum = 65536 if hidden_size <= 4096 else 16384
+    granularity = 1 if inference else 1024
+    if tokens <= 0 or tokens % granularity or tokens > maximum:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "shortcut fusion requires local flattened T to be a positive "
+            f"multiple of {granularity} "
+            f"and at most {maximum} for H={hidden_size}; got T={tokens}"
+        )
+    if residual.dtype not in (torch.float32, torch.bfloat16) or not residual.is_contiguous():
+        raise ValueError("shortcut fusion requires contiguous FP32 or BF16 residuals")
+    if not residual.is_cuda:
+        raise ValueError("shortcut fusion requires CUDA tensors")
+    return tokens
+
+
+class _Boundary(torch.autograd.Function):
+    """Own one boundary's tensors; no workspace or handoff is stored on a module."""
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def forward(ctx, options, consumer_weight, residual, *values):
+        streams, replay_manager, mxfp8_handoff, mxfp8_consumer, epsilon, update_count = options
+        from .forward_kernel import forward
+
+        # values: updates, write, retain, then one read and one gamma per reader.
+        count = (len(values) - 2 - update_count) // 2
+        updates = values[:update_count]
+        write, retain = values[update_count : update_count + 2]
+        reads = values[update_count + 2 : update_count + 2 + count]
+        gammas = values[update_count + 2 + count :]
+        hidden = updates[0].shape[-1]
+        validate_input(residual, hidden, streams, inference=ctx is None)
+        leading = residual.shape[:-1]
+        if any(t.shape != (*leading, hidden) for t in updates):
+            raise ValueError("shortcut updates must have the residual's leading dimensions")
+        current, saved, outputs = forward(
+            residual.view(-1, streams * hidden),
+            tuple(t.contiguous().view(-1, hidden) for t in updates),
+            write,
+            retain,
+            reads,
+            gammas,
+            mxfp8_handoff=mxfp8_handoff,
+            num_streams=streams,
+            epsilon=epsilon,
+            inference=ctx is None,
+        )
+        outputs = tuple(q.view(*leading, hidden) for q in outputs)
+        result = (current.view(*leading, streams * hidden), *outputs)
+        if ctx is None:
+            return result
+        ctx.replay_link = None
+        if replay_manager is not None:
+            ctx.replay_link = replay_manager.register(
+                residual, current, saved, prepare_columns=mxfp8_handoff
+            )
+        ctx.previous = (
+            ResidualSlot(residual) if ctx.replay_link is None else ctx.replay_link.previous_slot
+        )
+        # Save the predecessor even without recomputation. The backward never
+        # reconstructs it from a rounded successor.
+        ctx.save_for_backward(
+            residual, saved.update, saved.coefficients, *saved.gammas, *saved.rstd
+        )
+        ctx.boundary_spec = (
+            saved.controller_sizes,
+            saved.has_retention,
+            streams,
+            leading,
+            update_count,
+        )
+        ctx.mxfp8_reader = None
+        if mxfp8_handoff:
+            from .mxfp8_handoff import Reader
+
+            ctx.mxfp8_reader = Reader(outputs[0], saved, mxfp8_consumer)
+        ctx.set_materialize_grads(False)
+        return result
+
+    @staticmethod
+    @once_differentiable
+    def backward(ctx, carry, *dys):
+        from .backward_kernel import backward
+        from .kernel_utils import SavedWrite
+
+        sizes, has_retention, streams, leading, update_count = ctx.boundary_spec
+        previous, update, coefficients, *readers = ctx.saved_tensors
+        ctx.previous.ensure()
+        count = len(dys)
+        saved = SavedWrite(
+            update,
+            coefficients,
+            tuple(readers[:count]),
+            tuple(readers[count:]),
+            sizes,
+            num_streams=streams,
+            has_retention=has_retention,
+            num_updates=update_count,
+        )
+        hidden = update.shape[1]
+        previous = previous.view(-1, streams * hidden)
+        dy = tuple(None if t is None else t.contiguous().view(-1, hidden) for t in dys)
+        dc = None if carry is None else carry.contiguous().view_as(previous)
+        reader = ctx.mxfp8_reader
+        needs_columns = reader is not None and bool(reader.pending)
+        column = (
+            ctx.replay_link.columns() if needs_columns and ctx.replay_link is not None else None
+        )
+        columns = (column,) + (None,) * (count - 1)
+        grads, _ = backward(
+            saved,
+            previous,
+            dy,
+            dc,
+            save_columns=needs_columns,
+            columns=columns,
+            on_columns_ready=(
+                (lambda columns: reader.compute_wgrad(previous, columns[0]))
+                if needs_columns
+                else None
+            ),
+        )
+        if reader is not None:
+            reader.finish(previous)
+        # Preserve allocator publication for retained backwards while releasing
+        # interval tapes/columns once their final autograd consumer has returned.
+        ctx.previous = retained_slot(ctx.previous)
+        ctx.replay_link = None
+        grads = list(grads)
+        # A missing reader must not create gradients for its private controller
+        # or norm weight, even when the internal kernel materializes zero dy.
+        for index, grad in enumerate(dys):
+            if grad is None:
+                grads[update_count + 3 + index] = None
+                grads[update_count + 3 + count + index] = None
+        # Memoize views so shared update gradients preserve Tensor identity.
+        views = {}
+        for i, grad in enumerate(grads[: update_count + 1]):
+            if grad is not None:
+                if id(grad) not in views:
+                    views[id(grad)] = grad.view(*leading, streams * hidden if i == 0 else hidden)
+                grads[i] = views[id(grad)]
+        return (None, None) + tuple(
+            g if needed else None for g, needed in zip(grads, ctx.needs_input_grad[2:])
+        )
+
+
+@lru_cache
+def _trains_on(device_index: int) -> bool:
+    from .kernel_utils import qualified_device
+
+    return qualified_device(torch.cuda.get_device_properties(device_index))
+
+
+def _apply_boundary(
+    inputs, updates, *, num_streams, mxfp8_handoff=False, mxfp8_consumer=None, epsilon=1.0e-5
+):
+    mxfp8 = bool(mxfp8_handoff or mxfp8_consumer is not None)
+    if not torch.is_grad_enabled():
+        options = (num_streams, None, mxfp8, mxfp8_consumer, epsilon, updates)
+        return _Boundary.forward(None, options, None, *inputs)
+    if mxfp8_handoff and mxfp8_consumer is None:
+        raise ValueError("training shortcut MXFP8 requires an explicit deferred consumer")
+    residual = inputs[0]
+    if residual.is_cuda and not _trains_on(residual.device.index):
+        # Fail at the first boundary rather than after a whole forward pass.
+        raise ValueError(
+            "training through the fused shortcut seams requires a qualified GB300 (the fused "
+            f"backward is GB300-only); got {torch.cuda.get_device_name(residual.device)}"
+        )
+    # The explicit weight edge orders AccumulateGrad after the deferred TE wgrad.
+    options = (num_streams, current_manager(), mxfp8, mxfp8_consumer, epsilon, updates)
+    weight = None if mxfp8_consumer is None else mxfp8_consumer.weight
+    return _Boundary.apply(options, weight, *inputs)
+
+
+def wide_residual_write_read_rmsnorm_quant(residual, update, write, retain, read, gamma, **options):
+    """Fuse a compute-layer write and the shared expert's read/RMSNorm/quantization.
+
+    Keyword options require ``num_streams``. ``mxfp8_handoff`` defaults to False
+    and ``mxfp8_consumer`` to None.
+    ``epsilon`` is the RMSNorm epsilon and defaults to 1e-5.
+
+    ``mxfp8_handoff`` emits reader zero directly from FP32 into rowwise MXFP8;
+    TELinear automatically installs the saved-activation handoff after forward.
+    Its columnwise weight-gradient input is prepared during checkpoint replay,
+    or from the saved predecessor when checkpoint replay is disabled.
+
+    ``mxfp8_consumer`` also enables this format and declares that reader zero
+    is consumed exclusively by that Linear, with no other gradient-producing
+    uses. Its weight gradient must support deferral so the prepared column
+    operand can be handed to that consumer before parameter reductions.
+    Views passed to that same consumer are allowed.
+    Training MXFP8 calls require this consumer; standalone column reconstruction
+    is not supported. Unused residual and reader outputs are supported.
+    """
+    return _apply_boundary((residual, update, write, retain, read, gamma), 1, **options)
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class PendingShortcutAdd:
+    """A branch output not yet written to the wide residual.
+
+    The next layer's seam kernel writes it together with that layer's read/RMSNorm(s):
+    ``shortcut_add_wide_residual_write_two_reader_rmsnorm_quant`` for a fused shortcut block,
+    ``shortcut_add_wide_residual_write_read_rmsnorm_quant`` for a lone layer. A MoE output is a
+    shortcut add of ``routed`` and ``shared``; a single branch update (a lone layer's output)
+    leaves ``shared`` None. ``write``/``retain`` are the writing connection's logits
+    (``retain`` is None for fixed identity retention).
+    """
+
+    residual: torch.Tensor
+    routed: torch.Tensor
+    shared: torch.Tensor | None
+    write: torch.Tensor
+    retain: torch.Tensor | None
+
+
+def shortcut_add_wide_residual_write_two_reader_rmsnorm_quant(pending, reads, gammas, **options):
+    """Fuse a pending write and the next pair's two independent read/RMSNorms.
+
+    The write is a shortcut add (BF16 ``routed + shared``, as a MoE write) or, with
+    ``pending.shared`` None, a single update. MXFP8 options have the same exclusivity contract
+    as ``wide_residual_write_read_rmsnorm_quant``. Only reader zero uses MXFP8; the router
+    (reader one) remains BF16.
+    """
+    if len(reads) != 2 or len(gammas) != 2:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "shortcut_add_wide_residual_write_two_reader_rmsnorm_quant requires two read "
+            "controllers and two RMSNorm weights"
+        )
+    return _apply_pending(pending, reads, gammas, **options)
+
+
+def shortcut_add_wide_residual_write_read_rmsnorm_quant(pending, read, gamma, **options):
+    """Fuse a pending write and one following read/RMSNorm.
+
+    This is the seam into a lone layer: a fused block's MoE write (a shortcut add of
+    ``routed + shared``) or a lone layer's single update (``pending.shared`` None) is written
+    together with the next layer's input read and RMSNorm. Options and the MXFP8 contract
+    match ``wide_residual_write_read_rmsnorm_quant``.
+    """
+    return _apply_pending(pending, (read,), (gamma,), **options)
+
+
+def _apply_pending(pending, reads, gammas, **options):
+    p = pending
+    updates = (p.routed,) if p.shared is None else (p.routed, p.shared)
+    return _apply_boundary(
+        (p.residual, *updates, p.write, p.retain, *reads, *gammas), len(updates), **options
+    )

+# Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+"""Backward kernels for the aligned folded-reader forward graph.
+
+Read backward for configuration, allocation, launches, and final gradient reductions.
+_backward pipelines reader projections, predecessor reads and gradients within
+width-spanning groups, reusing shared slices as their consumers finish.
+"""
+
+from typing import NamedTuple
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+from triton.experimental import gluon as g
+from triton.experimental.gluon import language as gl
+from triton.experimental.gluon.language import BlockedLayout, SliceLayout, SwizzledSharedLayout
+from triton.experimental.gluon.language.nvidia.hopper import fence_async_shared, mbarrier, tma
+
+from .kernel_utils import (
+    FLAGSHIPS,
+    _descriptor,
+    _fma2,
+    qualified_device,
+    reduce_jobs,
+    validate_num_streams,
+)
+
+# Triton renamed this API in 3.9; both names use the same TMA operation.
+_tma_load = tma.async_load if hasattr(tma, "async_load") else tma.async_copy_global_to_shared
+
+_GRADIENT_LAYOUT = gl.constexpr(BlockedLayout([1, 4], [4, 8], [1, 4], [1, 0]))
+
+
+class _BackwardInputs(NamedTuple):
+    coefficients: object
+    rstd: tuple
+    gammas: tuple
+    carry: object
+    reader_grads: tuple
+
+
+class _BackwardOutputs(NamedTuple):
+    residual_grad: object
+    update_grad: object
+    controller_partials: object
+
+
+class _ReaderPartials(NamedTuple):
+    projection: object
+    gamma: tuple
+
+
+class _Geometry(NamedTuple):
+    M: int
+    H: int
+    STREAMS: int
+    HAS_RETENTION: bool
+
+
+class _BackwardConfig(NamedTuple):
+    """Projection-reduction layout, grid, register cap and Super one-reader early carry load."""
+
+    PROJECTION_ROWS_PER_WARP: int
+    PROJECTION_VECTOR: int
+    TARGET_CTAS: int
+    MAXNREG: int
+    EARLY_CARRY: bool = False
+
+
+def get_backward_knobs(m, h, streams, readers=1, *, grid="auto"):
+    """Select the launch knobs for one shape; an explicit grid overrides the auto grid."""
+    production = streams == 3 and (m, h) in FLAGSHIPS
+    rows = 2 if h == 4096 and streams not in (1, 4) else 4
+    vector = 4 if (h <= 3072 and not (h == 3072 and streams > 4)) or streams == 4 else 2
+    if streams == 3 and not production:
+        rows, vector = 8, 2 if h % 2048 else 4
+    budget = 456 if streams <= 3 else 288
+    if grid == "auto":
+        participants = triton.cdiv(h, 256)
+        grid = min(triton.cdiv(m, 16), max(1, budget // participants)) * participants
+    return _BackwardConfig(
+        PROJECTION_ROWS_PER_WARP=rows,
+        PROJECTION_VECTOR=vector,
+        TARGET_CTAS=grid,
+        EARLY_CARRY=production and h == 4096 and readers == 1,
+        # Six streams have less shared-memory residency; allow registers to avoid spills.
+        MAXNREG=255 if streams == 6 else 168,
+    )
+
+
+# Launch keys whose compile and residency check already passed.
+_RESIDENCY = {}
+
+
+@torch.no_grad()
+def backward(
+    saved,
+    previous,
+    dys,
+    carry=None,
+    *,
+    columns=None,
+    save_columns=False,
+    config="auto",
+    prepare_wgrad=None,
+    on_columns_ready=None,
+):
+    """Execute backward; both updates of a shortcut add share one gradient tensor.
+
+    Returns ``(grads, columns)``: grads holds the residual gradient, one update gradient per
+    branch update, the controller gradients (write, retain, then one read per reader) and one
+    RMSNorm weight gradient per reader. Only the reader count shapes the kernel.
+
+    Explicit config supports correctness/stress tests. on_columns_ready submits
+    dependent weight GEMMs before the fused kernel, which never reads the columns.
+    """
+    n, streams, updates = saved.reader_count, saved.num_streams, saved.update_count
+    m, h = saved.update.shape
+    validate_num_streams(streams)
+    if m <= 0 or m % 32 or h < 32 or h > 16384 or h % 32:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "shortcut backward requires positive rows divisible by 32 and H=32..16384, step 32"
+        )
+    if n not in (1, 2):
+        raise ValueError("backward requires one or two readers")
+    if updates not in (1, 2):
+        raise ValueError("backward requires one update, or two summed by a shortcut add")
+    if len(dys) != n:
+        raise ValueError("backward requires one gradient slot per reader")
+    if previous.dtype not in (torch.float32, torch.bfloat16):
+        raise ValueError("backward requires an FP32 or BF16 predecessor residual")
+    if carry is None:
+        carry = torch.zeros_like(previous)
+    if carry.dtype != previous.dtype:
+        raise ValueError("the residual gradient must have the residual's dtype")
+    dys = tuple(torch.zeros_like(saved.update) if dy is None else dy for dy in dys)
+    if not qualified_device(torch.cuda.get_device_properties(previous.device)):
+        raise ValueError("shortcut backward requires a qualified GB300")
+    # Resolve the column routes and build any missing column operands.
+    routes = prepare_wgrad
+    if routes is None:
+        routes = save_columns if config == "auto" else False
+    grid = config
+    nt = triton.cdiv(h, 256)
+    if grid != "auto" and (type(grid) is not int or grid <= 0 or grid % nt):
+        raise ValueError("shortcut grid must contain positive whole participant groups")
+    routes = (routes,) + (False,) * (n - 1) if isinstance(routes, bool) else routes
+    if len(routes) != n:
+        raise ValueError("shortcut backward requires one column route per reader")
+    columns = (None,) * n if columns is None else tuple(columns)
+    if len(columns) != n:
+        raise ValueError("one prebuilt column operand per reader is required")
+    missing = tuple(needed and column is None for needed, column in zip(routes, columns))
+    if any(missing):
+        from .replay_kernel import replay_columns
+
+        generated = replay_columns(previous, saved, readers=missing)
+        columns = tuple(old if old is not None else new for old, new in zip(columns, generated))
+    # The columns are complete and the kernel does not read them: submit the dependent
+    # weight GEMMs (and their reduce-scatters) first so communication overlaps the kernel.
+    if on_columns_ready is not None:
+        on_columns_ready(columns)
+    knobs = get_backward_knobs(m, h, streams, n, grid=grid)
+    grid = knobs.TARGET_CTAS
+    # Outputs and scratch belong to this invocation; a shortcut add's updates share one gradient.
+    empty = saved.coefficients.new_empty
+    du = empty((m, h), dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    grads = (
+        empty((m, streams * h), dtype=previous.dtype),
+        *((du,) * updates),
+        *(empty((size,)) if size else None for size in saved.controller_sizes),
+        *(empty((h,)) for _ in range(n)),
+    )
+    p = triton.cdiv(m, 16) * triton.cdiv(h, 128) * 8
+    gp = tuple(empty((triton.cdiv(m, 16), h)) for _ in range(n))
+    planes = (1 + n + saved.has_retention) * streams
+    controllers = empty((planes + n, p))
+    chunks = empty((planes + n, triton.cdiv(p, 1024)))
+
+    groups = grid // nt
+    tiles = triton.cdiv(m, 16)
+    if max(grid, tiles + 2 * groups, nt * (tiles + 1)) >= 2**31:
+        raise ValueError("arrival counter exceeds signed 32-bit capacity")
+    # Write-once handoff words (see _publish_word): one block per row tile, a
+    # 128-byte header (arrival hint, next-row-tile word) and one projection word per
+    # (reader, row, column tile). Every tagged word is written at most once per
+    # launch; each hint counts its row tile's producers. The admission and row-tile
+    # counters are the two int32 scheduler words.
+    block = 16 + n * 16 * nt
+    if tiles * block + 16 >= 2**31:
+        raise ValueError("handoff workspace exceeds signed 32-bit indexing")
+    # Separate allocations keep each workspace an ordinary invocation-owned tensor.
+    epochs = empty((2,), dtype=torch.int32)
+    pp = empty((tiles * block,), dtype=torch.int64)
+
+    slice_shape = (16, 128)
+    kw = dict(
+        inputs=_BackwardInputs(saved.coefficients, saved.rstd, saved.gammas, carry, dys),
+        GEOMETRY=_Geometry(m, h, streams, saved.has_retention),
+        CONFIG=_BackwardConfig(*(gl.constexpr(value) for value in knobs)),
+        partials=_ReaderPartials(pp, gp),
+        outputs=_BackwardOutputs(grads[0], grads[1], controllers),
+        scheduler=epochs,
+        CARRY_DESC=_descriptor(carry, slice_shape),
+        R_DESC=_descriptor(previous, slice_shape),
+        DY0_DESC=_descriptor(dys[0] if streams < 6 else None, slice_shape),
+        DY1_DESC=_descriptor(dys[1] if streams < 6 and n == 2 else None, slice_shape),
+        U_DESC=_descriptor(saved.update, slice_shape),
+        maxnreg=knobs.MAXNREG,
+        num_warps=4,
+        enable_fp_fusion=True,
+    )
+    # Compile and check residency once per specialization: the knobs carry the grid
+    # and every launch option; pointer-alignment variants share the shared-memory size.
+    key = (previous.device, previous.dtype, carry.dtype, saved.update.dtype)
+    key += (*(dy.dtype for dy in dys), m, h, streams, saved.has_retention, knobs)
+    if key not in _RESIDENCY:
+        kernel = _backward.warmup(**kw, grid=(grid,))
+        kernel._init_handles()
+        # Triton's cluster query assumes 128 threads, matching num_warps=4.
+        # Ticket admission needs one complete participant group, not the grid.
+        limit = triton.runtime.driver.active.utils.cuOccupancyMaxActiveClusters(
+            kernel.function, kernel.metadata.shared, 1
+        )
+        if nt > limit:
+            raise ValueError(f"required residency {nt} exceeds capacity: {limit}")
+        _RESIDENCY[key] = limit
+    # Reset on every invocation, including graph replay: every handoff word must
+    # start with tag 0 so an old launch's word can never satisfy a current poll.
+    # Stream order makes this memset visible to the whole kernel.
+    epochs.zero_()
+    pp.zero_()
+    _backward[(grid,)](**kw)
+    # Reduce controller chunks, then all gamma and controller gradients.
+    retention, two = saved.has_retention, n == 2
+
+    def plane(index):
+        return chunks[index * streams : (index + 1) * streams]
+
+    def coefficients(index):
+        return saved.coefficients[index * streams : (index + 1) * streams]
+
+    raw_b = planes  # Each reader's raw b row follows every controller plane.
+    beta0, beta1 = coefficients(2), coefficients(3) if two else None
+    write, retain = coefficients(0), coefficients(1) if retention else None
+    # Per controller (write, retention, then each reader's read): its partial plane
+    # and the raw rows/coefficients its final reduction combines. The raw write
+    # partial is sum(u * incoming_s); reader terms use the raw b rows only here.
+    kinds = (
+        (0, (chunks[raw_b], beta0, chunks[raw_b + 1] if two else None, beta1, True)),
+        (1, (plane(2), beta0, plane(3) if two else None, beta1) if retention else None),
+        *((1 + retention + r, (chunks[raw_b + r], write, retain)) for r in range(n)),
+    )
+    final = [(p, g, 0, 8, 0, None) for p, g in zip(gp, grads[-n:])]
+    for kind, (output, (index, combo)) in enumerate(
+        zip(grads[1 + updates : 3 + updates + n], kinds)
+    ):
+        if output is not None:
+            final.append((plane(index), output, 1, 1, 0, coefficients(4 + kind), combo))
+    reduce_jobs([(controllers, chunks, 1, 1, 1024, None)])
+    reduce_jobs(final)
+
+    return grads, columns
+
+
+# Backward arithmetic, partial reductions, and pipeline scheduling.
+
+
+# Fence-free cross-CTA handoff (projection partials and the next row tile).
+#
+# Each handoff value travels in one naturally aligned 64-bit word:
+#     word = value_bits | tag << 32,  tag = row_tile + 1 (never 0).
+# Memory-model argument (PTX ISA memory consistency model):
+# 1. Write-once: words are indexed by row tile, and each row tile is processed by
+#    exactly one group (initial tile = group index, later tiles from the atomic
+#    row-tile counter), so every word has at most one producer store per launch and
+#    is never reused within a launch: no write-after-read hazard, no ring buffer.
+# 2. Initial value: the host zeroes all words before every launch (also captured in
+#    CUDA graphs); stream order makes tag 0 the only prior value any thread sees.
+# 3. Atomicity: the producer's st.relaxed.gpu.b64 and the consumer's strong loads
+#    (ld.relaxed.gpu.b64, or ld.volatile = ld.relaxed.sys, possibly as a vector whose
+#    64-bit elements are each a scalar access) are morally strong: both strong,
+#    scopes containing both CTAs, same naturally aligned 8 bytes. So each load
+#    returns either the zero word or the complete produced word; seeing the
+#    expected tag implies seeing the value stored with it.
+# 4. No other data crosses CTAs inside this kernel (dR, du, gamma and controller
+#    partials are consumed by later launches), so no release/acquire fence is
+#    needed. In particular, no MEMBAR.GPU waits for the previous tile's dR/du stores.
+# 5. The per-row-tile arrival count (relaxed red.add, no fence) and the L2 warm-up
+#    of each claimed row tile's block are performance hints only: the hint is not
+#    ordered after the words, so consumers still check the tag of every register
+#    copy they sum, reloading any word that lags. Correctness never depends on them.
+#    A layout that replicates words across threads must check each thread's own
+#    copies: a CTA-wide reduction counts only one replica, and every replica stores
+#    its row sums (see the projection reduction in _backward).
+# 6. Progress: strong stores become visible eventually, and a group's CTAs are
+#    co-resident by ticket admission.
+
+
+@g.jit
+def _publish_word(pointer, value, tag, OWNER_MASK: gl.constexpr):
+    """Store value|tag<<32 once from threads whose (tid & OWNER_MASK) == 0."""
+    return gl.inline_asm_elementwise(
+        """
+        { // Begin write-once handoff publication.
+            .reg .pred owner; // Select one thread per distinct replicated value.
+            .reg .u32 tid; // CTA thread index.
+            .reg .b64 word; // Tagged 64-bit handoff word.
+            mov.u32 tid,%tid.x; // Read this thread's index.
+            and.b32 tid,tid,$4; // Keep the bits that index layout replicas.
+            setp.eq.u32 owner,tid,0; // Replica zero owns the store.
+            mov.b64 word,{$2,$3}; // Low half: value bits; high half: nonzero tag.
+            @owner st.relaxed.gpu.global.b64 [$1],word; // Single-copy-atomic publish, no fence.
+            mov.u32 $0,0; // Provide the required dummy output.
+        } // End write-once handoff publication.
+        """,
+        "=r,l,r,r,n",
+        [pointer, value, tag, OWNER_MASK],
+        dtype=gl.int32,
+        is_pure=False,
+        pack=1,
+    )
+
+
+@g.jit
+def _arrive_hint(pointer):
+    """Count this CTA's publication with one relaxed reduction (no fence)."""
+    return gl.inline_asm_elementwise(
+        """
+        { // Begin arrival hint.
+            .reg .pred leader; // One thread per CTA counts the arrival.
+            .reg .u32 tid; // CTA thread index.
+            mov.u32 tid,%tid.x; // Read this thread's index.
+            setp.eq.u32 leader,tid,0; // Thread zero is the leader.
+            @leader red.relaxed.gpu.global.add.u32 [$1],1; // Hint only: orders nothing.
+            mov.u32 $0,0; // Provide the required dummy output.
+        } // End arrival hint.
+        """,
+        "=r,l",
+        [pointer],
+        dtype=gl.int32,
+        is_pure=False,
+        pack=1,
+    )
+
+
+@g.jit
+def _await_hint(pointer, expected):
+    """Spin until the arrival hint reaches expected. Performance only: the tagged
+    words are verified afterwards, so a hint seen before its CTA's words is safe."""
+    return gl.inline_asm_elementwise(
+        """
+        { // Begin arrival-hint poll; labels are local to this scope.
+            .reg .pred ready; // Whether every producer CTA has arrived.
+            .reg .u32 count; // Observed arrival count.
+        WAIT: // Poll one scalar per warp.
+            ld.relaxed.gpu.global.u32 count,[$1]; // Strong GPU-scope load of the hint.
+            setp.ge.u32 ready,count,$2; // Compare with the participant count.
+            @!ready bra WAIT; // Keep polling until all producers arrived.
+            mov.u32 $0,count; // Return the observed count.
+        } // End arrival-hint poll.
+        """,
+        "=r,l,n",
+        [pointer, expected],
+        dtype=gl.int32,
+        is_pure=False,
+        pack=1,
+    )
+
+
+@g.jit
+def _verify_word(word, pointer, tag):
+    """Return word once its high half equals tag, re-polling only this thread's lagging word.
+
+    Every thread checks its own copies: the consumer layout may replicate a word across
+    warps, and a CTA-wide reduction counts only one replica of each element."""
+    return gl.inline_asm_elementwise(
+        """
+        { // Begin per-thread handoff verification; labels are local to this scope.
+            .reg .pred ready; // Whether the observed tag is the expected one.
+            .reg .b32 value,seen; // Low and high halves of the observed word.
+            .reg .b64 word; // Most recently observed word.
+            mov.b64 word,$1; // Start from the vector load (usually ready).
+        CHECK: // Re-examine the most recent observation.
+            mov.b64 {value,seen},word; // Split the single-copy-atomic word.
+            setp.eq.u32 ready,seen,$3; // The producer's tag implies its value.
+            @ready bra DONE; // Use the value stored together with the tag.
+            ld.relaxed.gpu.global.b64 word,[$2]; // Re-poll this word with a strong load.
+            bra CHECK; // Check the new observation.
+        DONE: // The word is the producer's word for this tag.
+            mov.b64 $0,word; // Return the verified word.
+        } // End per-thread handoff verification.
+        """,
+        "=l,l,l,r",
+        [word, pointer, tag],
+        dtype=gl.int64,
+        is_pure=False,
+        pack=1,
+    )
+
+
+@g.jit
+def _missing_words(w0, w1, tag, TWO: gl.constexpr):
+    """Count words (both readers, whole CTA) whose tag is not yet the expected one."""
+    missing = gl.where((w0 >> 32).to(gl.int32) == tag, 0, 1)
+    if TWO:
+        missing += gl.where((w1 >> 32).to(gl.int32) == tag, 0, 1)
+    return gl.sum(gl.sum(missing, 1), 0)
+
+
+@g.jit
+def _bulk_prefetch_l2(pointer, valid, BYTES: gl.constexpr, THREADS: gl.constexpr):
+    """Warm BYTES at pointer in L2 from each valid thread below THREADS (a hint only)."""
+    return gl.inline_asm_elementwise(
+        """
+        { // Begin L2 bulk prefetch.
+            .reg .pred p,owner; // Declare validity and ownership predicates.
+            .reg .u32 tid; // Declare the CTA thread index.
+            mov.u32 tid,%tid.x; // Read this thread's index.
+            setp.lt.u32 owner,tid,$4; // Select the issuing threads.
+            setp.ne.u32 p,$2,0; // Check the validity mask.
+            and.pred p,p,owner; // Require both validity and ownership.
+            @p cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2.global [$1],$3; // Warm the range in L2.
+            mov.u32 $0,0; // Provide the required dummy output.
+        } // End L2 bulk prefetch.
+        """,
+        "=r,l,r,n,n",
+        [pointer, valid, BYTES, THREADS],
+        dtype=gl.int32,
+        is_pure=False,
+        pack=1,
+    )
+
+
+@g.jit
+def _await_word(word, pointer, tag):
+    """Return the low 32 bits of the word once its high half equals tag."""
+    return gl.inline_asm_elementwise(
+        """
+        { // Begin handoff poll; labels are local to this scope.
+            .reg .pred ready; // Whether the observed tag is the expected one.
+            .reg .b32 value,seen; // Low and high halves of the observed word.
+            .reg .b64 word; // Most recently observed word.
+            mov.b64 word,$1; // Start from the optimistic load (usually ready).
+        POLL: // Re-examine the most recent observation.
+            mov.b64 {value,seen},word; // Split the single-copy-atomic word.
+            setp.eq.u32 ready,seen,$3; // The producer's tag implies its value.
+            @ready bra DONE; // Use the value stored together with the tag.
+            ld.relaxed.gpu.global.b64 word,[$2]; // Re-poll with a strong GPU-scope load.
+            bra POLL; // Check the new observation.
+        DONE: // The value is the producer's value for this tag.
+            mov.b32 $0,value; // Return the value bits.
+        } // End handoff poll.
+        """,
+        "=r,l,l,r",
+        [word, pointer, tag],
+        dtype=gl.int32,
+        is_pure=False,
+        pack=1,
+    )
+
+
+@g.jit
+def _mul2(a, b):
+    # Pair adjacent independent raw-dot products; preserve each FP32 RN result.
+    return gl.inline_asm_elementwise(
+        """
+        {
+            .reg .b64 a,b,r;
+            mov.b64 a,{$2,$3};
+            mov.b64 b,{$4,$5};
+            mul.rn.f32x2 r,a,b;
+            mov.b64 {$0,$1},r;
+        }
+        """,
+        "=f,=f,f,f,f,f",
+        [a, b],
+        dtype=gl.float32,
+        is_pure=True,
+        pack=2,
+    )
+
+
+@g.jit
+def _store_controller(destination, value, valid):
+    """Reduce each 16×128 slice into eight fixed lane-group controller partials."""
+    owned = gl.permute(gl.reshape(value, (4, 4, 4, 8, 4)), (2, 1, 3, 0, 4))
+    per_thread = gl.sum(gl.reshape(owned, (128, 16)), 1)
+    total = gl.sum(gl.reshape(per_thread, (8, 16)), 1)
+    gl.store(destination + gl.arange(0, 8, layout=total.type.layout), total, valid)
+
+
+@g.jit
+def _widen_bf16(x):
+    # Exact widening to FP32; BF16 bits become the upper half of the FP32 word.
+    if x.dtype == gl.bfloat16:
+        return (x.to(gl.uint16, bitcast=True).to(gl.uint32) << 16).to(gl.float32, bitcast=True)
+    return x.to(gl.float32)
+
+
+@g.jit
+def _thread_pairs(value):
+    """Eight per-thread (128, 2) column pairs of a 16x128 slice, in _store_controller order."""
+    owned = gl.permute(gl.reshape(value, (4, 4, 4, 8, 4)), (2, 1, 3, 0, 4))
+    # Per-thread index a*4 + e = (a_hi, a_lo, e_hi, e_lo); e_lo pairs adjacent columns.
+    t = gl.reshape(owned, (128, 2, 2, 2, 2))
+    e_hi0, e_hi1 = gl.split(gl.permute(t, (0, 1, 2, 4, 3)))
+    pairs = ()
+    for half in gl.static_range(2):
+        rest = e_hi0 if half == 0 else e_hi1
+        a_lo0, a_lo1 = gl.split(gl.permute(rest, (0, 1, 3, 2)))
+        for quarter in gl.static_range(2):
+            a_hi0, a_hi1 = gl.split(gl.permute(a_lo0 if quarter == 0 else a_lo1, (0, 2, 1)))
+            pairs += (a_hi0, a_hi1)
+    return pairs
+
+
+@g.jit
+def _store_controller_dot(destination, a, b, valid):
+    """_store_controller(destination, a * b, valid) with one packed FMA chain per thread.
+
+    Each thread accumulates its 16 products in two column lanes (eight fma.rn.f32x2) and
+    adds the lanes; the lane-group reduction and the eight partial slots are unchanged.
+    """
+    pa = _thread_pairs(a)
+    pb = _thread_pairs(b)
+    acc = _mul2(pa[0], pb[0])
+    for k in gl.static_range(1, 8):
+        acc = _fma2(pa[k], pb[k], acc)
+    per_thread = gl.sum(acc, 1)
+    total = gl.sum(gl.reshape(per_thread, (8, 16)), 1)
+    gl.store(destination + gl.arange(0, 8, layout=total.type.layout), total, valid)
+
+
+@g.jit
+def _coefficient(cs, index):
+    indices = gl.full((1,), index, gl.int32, gl.constexpr(BlockedLayout([1], [32], [4], [0])))
+    return gl.sum(cs.gather(indices, 0), 0)
+
+
+@g.jit
+def _partial_offset(reader, rr, cc, NT: gl.constexpr):
+    TILE: gl.constexpr = min(16, NT & -NT)
+    return reader * 16 * NT + (cc // TILE * 16 + rr) * TILE + cc % TILE
+
+
+@g.jit
+def _prefetch(P, rp, cp, GEOMETRY: gl.constexpr):
+    """Warm this tile's carry rows in L2 without replacing any TMA wait."""
+    m: gl.constexpr = GEOMETRY.M
+    h: gl.constexpr = GEOMETRY.H
+    streams: gl.constexpr = GEOMETRY.STREAMS
+    # One thread per row warms the row's 256 columns of each stream.
+    ROWS: gl.constexpr = 16
+    ELEMENT: gl.constexpr = P.dtype.element_ty.primitive_bitwidth // 8
+    ROW_BYTES: gl.constexpr = 256 * ELEMENT
+    i = gl.arange(0, ROWS, layout=gl.constexpr(BlockedLayout([1], [32], [4], [0])))
+    rr = rp * 16 + i
+    cc = cp * 256
+    base = P + rr * (streams * h) + cc
+    # Stream zero is loaded directly, without a bootstrap transfer, so warm every stream.
+    for stream in gl.static_range(streams):
+        valid = rr < m
+        if h % 256:
+            # Keep prefetch hints within the logical residual stream.
+            valid &= cc + 256 <= h
+        _bulk_prefetch_l2(base + stream * h, valid.to(gl.int32), ROW_BYTES, ROWS)
+        if h % 256:
+            # Preserve the original single 128-column hint at a short final tile.
+            # Full rows use one 1024-byte request instead of two 512-byte requests.
+            tail = (rr < m) & (cc + 128 <= h) & (cc + 256 > h)
+            _bulk_prefetch_l2(base + stream * h, tail.to(gl.int32), 128 * ELEMENT, ROWS)
+
+
+@g.jit
+def _copy_tiles(plan, row_tile, barrier, part: gl.constexpr):
+    """Copy column half part of each slice into its rows of the [32, 128] storage."""
+    for i in gl.static_range(len(plan)):
+        descriptor, tile, column = plan[i]
+        tile = tile.slice(part * 16, 16)
+        _tma_load(descriptor, [row_tile * 16, column + part * 128], barrier, tile)
+
+
+@g.jit
+def _refill_slice(
+    s: gl.constexpr,
+    carry_copies,
+    residual_copies,
+    barriers,
+    copy_barrier,
+    row_tile,
+    next_rp,
+    part: gl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Refill consumed predecessor slice s with carry s + 1, or the next tile's last stream."""
+    if s + 1 < len(residual_copies):
+        bits: gl.constexpr = carry_copies[s][0].dtype.primitive_bitwidth
+        mbarrier.expect(barriers[s], 16 * 128 * bits // 8)
+        _copy_tiles((carry_copies[s],), row_tile, barriers[s], part)
+    else:
+        _copy_tiles((residual_copies[s],), next_rp, copy_barrier, part)
+
+
+@g.jit
+def _load_residual(residuals, cols, part, stream: gl.constexpr, h: gl.constexpr):
+    # A BF16 residual is widened exactly; every product and sum below runs in FP32.
+    value = _widen_bf16(residuals[stream].slice(part * 16, 16).load(_GRADIENT_LAYOUT))
+    if h % 256:
+        value = gl.where(cols < h, value, 0)
+    return value
+
+
+@g.jit
+def _reader_partials(
+    inputs,
+    partials,
+    residuals,
+    ds,
+    update_shared,
+    gs,
+    cs,
+    projection_words,
+    tag,
+    rs0,
+    rs1,
+    row_tile,
+    column_tile,
+    cc,
+    GEOMETRY: gl.constexpr,
+    ctas_per_group: gl.constexpr,
+    half_barrier,
+    phase,
+    deps,
+):
+    """Projection and gamma partials of one or two readers, one 16x128 half at a time.
+
+    The caller has waited for half zero; half one's transfer (the last one issued by
+    the previous tile) completes on half_barrier while half zero is reduced.
+
+    Each half is consumed directly in the gradient layout L (no logical [16,256]
+    reshape or layout conversion). Every R/U element is read from shared memory
+    once and feeds both readers' FMAs in forward order:
+        x_r = sum_s fma(beta_r[s] * t[s], R_s, x_r);  x_r = fma(q_r, u, x_r)
+    Projection: each thread accumulates dz*z over both halves, then one row sum.
+    Gamma partials sum dy*z over the 16 rows of each half.
+
+    With one reader, reader one's loads alias reader zero's (rs1 = rs0, slice zero of
+    dy and gamma) and its stores are skipped, so every reader-one value is dead and
+    compiled out: the single reader keeps exactly its own FMA order.
+    """
+    TWO: gl.constexpr = len(inputs.reader_grads) == 2
+    m: gl.constexpr = GEOMETRY.M
+    h: gl.constexpr = GEOMETRY.H
+    streams: gl.constexpr = GEOMETRY.STREAMS
+    retention: gl.constexpr = GEOMETRY.HAS_RETENTION
+    L: gl.constexpr = _GRADIENT_LAYOUT
+    # Folded reader coefficients alpha_r[s] = FP32(beta_r[s] * t[s]) and the rounded
+    # update mix q_r = sum_fma(beta_r[s] * w[s]), as in forward and the gradient phase.
+    alpha0, alpha1 = (), ()
+    mix0 = 0.0
+    mix1 = 0.0
+    for s in gl.static_range(streams):
+        retain = _coefficient(cs, streams + s) if retention else 1.0
+        write = _coefficient(cs, s)
+        beta0 = _coefficient(cs, 2 * streams + s)
+        beta1 = _coefficient(cs, 3 * streams + s)
+        alpha0 += (beta0 * retain,)
+        alpha1 += (beta1 * retain,)
+        mix0 = gl.fma(beta0, write, mix0)
+        mix1 = gl.fma(beta1, write, mix1)
+    kr = gl.arange(0, 16, layout=gl.constexpr(SliceLayout(1, L)))
+    rows = (row_tile * 16 + kr)[:, None]
+    r0 = rs0[:, None]
+    r1 = rs1[:, None]
+    projection0 = gl.full((16, 128), 0, gl.float32, L)
+    projection1 = gl.full((16, 128), 0, gl.float32, L)
+    for part in gl.static_range(2):
+        if part == 1:
+            mbarrier.wait(half_barrier, phase, deps=deps)
+        cols = (cc + part * 128)[None, :]
+        mask = rows < m
+        if h % 256:
+            mask &= cols < h
+        offset = rows * h + cols
+        u = update_shared.slice(part * 16, 16).load(L).to(gl.float32)
+        x0 = gl.full((16, 128), 0, gl.float32, L)
+        x1 = gl.full((16, 128), 0, gl.float32, L)
+        for s in gl.static_range(streams):
+            rv = _load_residual(residuals, cols, part, s, h)
+            x0 = _fma2(alpha0[s], rv, x0)
+            x1 = _fma2(alpha1[s], rv, x1)
+        x0 = _fma2(mix0, u, x0)
+        x1 = _fma2(mix1, u, x1)
+        # z[j] = r * x[j]
+        z0 = x0 * r0
+        z1 = x1 * r1
+        if ds is None:
+            dy0 = gl.load(inputs.reader_grads[0] + offset, mask, 0).to(gl.float32)
+            dy1 = gl.load(inputs.reader_grads[-1] + offset, mask, 0).to(gl.float32)
+        else:
+            dy0 = ds.slice(part * 16, 16).load(L).to(gl.float32)
+            dy1 = ds.slice(TWO * 32 + part * 16, 16).load(L).to(gl.float32)
+        gamma0 = gs.slice(part * 128, 128).load(gl.constexpr(SliceLayout(0, L)))[None, :]
+        gamma1 = gs.slice(TWO * 256 + part * 128, 128).load(gl.constexpr(SliceLayout(0, L)))
+        gamma1 = gamma1[None, :]
+        # dz[j] = dy[j] * gamma[j]; accumulate dz*z per element across both halves.
+        projection0 += (dy0 * gamma0) * z0
+        projection1 += (dy1 * gamma1) * z1
+        # Gamma partials: sum over this tile's 16 rows of dy*z.
+        gamma_mask = row_tile * 16 < m
+        if h % 256:
+            gamma_mask &= cc + part * 128 < h
+        gamma_cols = row_tile * h + cc + part * 128
+        gl.store(partials.gamma[0] + gamma_cols, gl.sum(dy0 * z0, 0), gamma_mask)
+        if TWO:
+            gl.store(partials.gamma[1] + gamma_cols, gl.sum(dy1 * z1, 0), gamma_mask)
+    # Projection partials p_r = sum_j(dz[j] * z[j]) / H over this CTA's 256 columns.
+    # Publish as write-once tagged words (see _publish_word). In SliceLayout(1, L) each
+    # row's sum is replicated over the 8 column lanes (tid bits 0-2) and the 4 column
+    # warps (tid bits 5-6); replica zero (tid & 0x67 == 0) publishes.
+    OWNER_MASK: gl.constexpr = 7 | (3 << 5)
+    # Within the row tile's block, each reader owns 16 x NT words.
+    _publish_word(
+        projection_words + _partial_offset(0, kr, column_tile, ctas_per_group),
+        (gl.sum(projection0, 1) / h).to(gl.int32, bitcast=True),
+        tag,
+        OWNER_MASK,
+    )
+    if TWO:
+        _publish_word(
+            projection_words + _partial_offset(1, kr, column_tile, ctas_per_group),
+            (gl.sum(projection1, 1) / h).to(gl.int32, bitcast=True),
+            tag,
+            OWNER_MASK,
+        )
+
+
+@g.jit
+def _backward(
+    inputs,
+    partials,
+    outputs,
+    scheduler,
+    GEOMETRY: gl.constexpr,

+        cfg = _ForwardConfig(min(width, 8192), 0, 0, readers == 2, 0, 16)
+    replicas = min(8, 128 // triton.next_power_of_2(m)) if inference and m <= 64 else 1
+    split = replicas > 1 and readers == 2
+    # Whole 32-column groups keep both data and MXFP8 scale ownership exhaustive.
+    parts = min(replicas // (1 + split), (h // 32) & -(h // 32)) if h % 32 == 0 else 1
+    return cfg._replace(PARTS=parts, SPLIT=split)
+
+
+@torch.no_grad()
+def forward(
+    residual,
+    updates,
+    write,
+    retain,
+    reads,
+    gammas,
+    *,
+    mxfp8_handoff=False,
+    num_streams=3,
+    epsilon=1.0e-5,
+    inference=False,
+):
+    """Write the current residual and the folded RMSNorm reader operands.
+
+    One or two readers (``reads``/``gammas``) consume the write of one update, or of a
+    shortcut add of two updates. Inference skips backward state
+    (coefficients, the shortcut add's BF16 update sum and reader statistics), returning
+    saved=None. A shortcut add rounds its BF16 update sum before writing the residual.
+    The residual is FP32 or BF16 (the current residual keeps its dtype) and controller logits
+    are FP32 or BF16; every value is widened to FP32 for the arithmetic, a BF16 residual is
+    rounded only when stored, and readers fold the unrounded FP32 values.
+    Operands belong to forward consumers, not the tape. The exclusive MXFP8
+    handoff quantizes reader zero; every other reader returns BF16.
+    Widths divisible by four use packet loads and require a 16-byte-aligned FP32 residual base.
+
+    retain=None means fixed identity retention (t=1), not zero logits (t=0.95).
+    This static mode removes retention arithmetic and its parameter gradient.
+    A supplied tensor always keeps the learned path, regardless of its values.
+
+    Args:
+        residual: Previous FP32 or BF16 residual, ``[M, num_streams * H]``.
+        updates: One BF16 branch update, or two summed by a shortcut add, each ``[M, H]``.
+        write: FP32 or BF16 write-gate logits.
+        retain: FP32 or BF16 retention logits, or None for fixed identity retention.
+        reads: FP32 or BF16 mixing logits, one tensor per reader.
+        gammas: BF16 RMSNorm weights, one ``[H]`` tensor per reader.
+        mxfp8_handoff: Quantize reader 0 to rowwise MXFP8.
+        num_streams: Residual streams.
+        epsilon: RMSNorm epsilon.
+        inference: Skip backward state and use the inference schedules.
+
+    Returns:
+        ``(current residual, saved write, consumer operands)``; saved write is None in
+        inference.
+
+    Raises:
+        ValueError: If the inputs' counts, shapes, devices or MXFP8 alignment are invalid.
+    """
+    validate_num_streams(num_streams)
+    n = len(reads)
+    if n not in (1, 2) or len(gammas) != n or len(updates) not in (1, 2):
+        raise ValueError("one or two readers write one update or a shortcut add of two")
+    shortcut_add = len(updates) == 2
+    if not residual.is_cuda or updates[0].ndim != 2:
+        raise ValueError("expected CUDA [M,H] updates")
+    m, h = updates[0].shape
+    if m <= 0 or h <= 0:
+        raise ValueError("forward requires positive rows and width")
+    device = residual.device
+    if residual.dtype not in (torch.float32, torch.bfloat16):
+        raise ValueError("the residual must be FP32 or BF16")
+    _tensor(residual, (m, num_streams * h), residual.dtype, device, "residual")
+    for u in updates:
+        _tensor(u, (m, h), torch.bfloat16, device, "update")
+    for controller in (write, *((retain,) if retain is not None else ()), *reads):
+        if controller.ndim != 1 or controller.numel() < num_streams:
+            raise ValueError(f"controllers require at least {num_streams} entries")
+        if controller.dtype not in (torch.float32, torch.bfloat16):
+            raise ValueError("controller logits must be FP32 or BF16")
+        _tensor(controller, controller.shape, controller.dtype, device, "controller")
+    for gamma in gammas:
+        _tensor(gamma, (h,), torch.bfloat16, device, "gamma")
+    config = choose_forward_config(
+        _BATCH_INVARIANT_ROWS if inference and _batch_invariant_mode() else m,
+        h,
+        num_streams,
+        n,
+        mxfp8=mxfp8_handoff,
+        inference=inference,
+        updates=len(updates),
+        bf16_residual=residual.dtype == torch.bfloat16,
+    )
+    if not inference and (config.PARTS != 1 or config.SPLIT):
+        # The saved coefficients and per-reader rstd have one writer per row (a cluster's lead
+        # CTA); replicated parts and split readers would overwrite them.
+        raise RuntimeError(f"training forward needs PARTS == 1 and no SPLIT, got {config}")
+    c = None if inference else torch.empty((8 * num_streams,), device=device, dtype=torch.float32)
+
+    if type(residual).__name__ not in ("FakeTensor", "FunctionalTensor"):
+        # FP32 residual packets are 16-byte vector loads. Training also saves the residual and
+        # updates for the backward, which reads them through 16-byte-aligned TMA descriptors (for
+        # the shapes the backward accepts: rows and H divisible by 32).
+        packets = h % 4 == 0 and residual.dtype == torch.float32
+        tma = not inference and m % 32 == 0 and h % 32 == 0
+        aligned = ((residual,) if packets or tma else ()) + (tuple(updates) if tma else ())
+        if any(t.data_ptr() % 16 for t in aligned):
+            raise ValueError(
+                "the residual (FP32 packets, training) and training updates must be 16-byte "
+                "aligned"
+            )
+    if mxfp8_handoff and (m % 32 or h % 32):
+        raise ValueError("MXFP8 handoff requires rows and hidden width divisible by 32")
+
+    output_bf16 = (False, True)[:n] if mxfp8_handoff else (True,) * n
+    current = torch.empty_like(residual)
+    summed = torch.empty_like(updates[0]) if shortcut_add and not inference else None
+    stats = tuple(
+        None if inference else torch.empty(m, dtype=torch.float32, device=device) for _ in range(n)
+    )
+    qs = []
+    for output_is_bf16 in output_bf16:
+        q = allocate_operand((m, h), device, output_is_bf16)
+        # Inference fills padded rows in-kernel; partial scale columns still need clearing.
+        if not output_is_bf16 and (h % 128 or (m % 128 and not inference)):
+            q._rowwise_scale_inv.zero_()
+        qs.append(q)
+
+    saved = (
+        None
+        if inference
+        else SavedWrite(
+            summed if summed is not None else updates[0].detach(),
+            c,
+            tuple(gamma.detach() for gamma in gammas),
+            stats,
+            tuple(0 if v is None else v.numel() for v in (write, retain, *reads)),
+            num_streams,
+            retain is not None,
+            len(updates),
+        )
+    )
+    # A runtime unit retention coefficient preserves Ultra register occupancy.
+    # Short rows duplicate reductions for occupancy; stores have one owner.
+    dependent = inference and _programmatic_launch(device)
+    grid = (m, 2 if config.SPLIT else 1, config.PARTS)
+    write_args = _WriteArgs(
+        residual, updates[0], updates[1] if shortcut_add else None, current, summed
+    )
+    kwargs = dict(
+        read_tensors=_ReadArgs(gammas, stats, *operand_buffers(qs, columnwise=False)),
+        GEOMETRY=_Geometry(h, num_streams, retain is not None or h == 10240),
+        EPSILON=epsilon,
+        controllers=_ControllerArgs(write, retain, reads[0], reads[-1]),
+        saved_coefficients=c,
+        PAD_ROWS=inference and mxfp8_handoff and bool(m % 128),
+        DEPENDENT=dependent,
+        enable_fp_fusion=False,
+        # Inference launches as a programmatic dependent: the grid may start while the
+        # previous kernel drains, reads only parameters (and prefetches into L2), then waits for
+        # it (griddepcontrol.wait) before touching the previous kernel's outputs.
+        launch_pdl=dependent,
+    )
+    if config.CLUSTER > 1:
+        cluster = dict(
+            CONFIG=config,
+            EXCHANGE=_exchange_asm(config.CLUSTER, 1 if config.SPLIT else n),
+            num_warps=config.NUM_WARPS,
+            maxnreg=config.MAXNREG,
+        )
+        if _programmatic_launch(device) and _as_cluster(
+            write_args, grid, config.CLUSTER, kwargs | cluster
+        ):
+            _forward[grid](write_args, **kwargs, **cluster)
+            return current, saved, tuple(qs)
+        config = config._replace(CLUSTER=1)  # same slices, one CTA per row
+    _forward[grid](
+        write_args, CONFIG=config, num_warps=config.NUM_WARPS, maxnreg=config.MAXNREG, **kwargs
+    )
+    return current, saved, tuple(qs)
+
+
+def _as_cluster(write_args, grid, ctas, kwargs):
+    """Make ``_forward``'s compiled kernel for these arguments launch as clusters of CTAs.
+
+    ``_forward`` compiles as a single-CTA kernel; Triton's launcher runs gridX * num_ctas CTAs
+    in clusters of num_ctas along x, taking num_ctas from the packed (warps, ctas, shared)
+    metadata. That layout is private to Triton (checked against 3.7.0 and 3.7.1); an exchange
+    without its cluster peers would never complete, so an unexpected metadata form makes the
+    caller launch without a cluster.
+
+    Args:
+        write_args: ``_WriteArgs`` of the launch.
+        grid: Launch grid; x is the row count.
+        ctas: CTAs per cluster.
+        kwargs: The launch's remaining keyword arguments.
+
+    Returns:
+        True if the kernel will launch as clusters of ``ctas`` CTAs, False otherwise.
+    """
+    kernel = _forward.warmup(write_args, grid=grid, **kwargs)
+    meta = kernel.packed_metadata
+    if not (isinstance(meta, tuple) and len(meta) == 3 and meta[1] in (1, ctas)):
+        return False
+    kernel.packed_metadata = (meta[0], ctas, meta[2])
+    return True
+
+
+def _exchange_asm(ctas, partials):
+    """Return the PTX for a cluster's partial-sum exchange (sm_90+).
+
+    Gluon (Triton 3.7.1) cannot address a peer CTA's shared memory, so the exchange is PTX
+    with its own static shared barrier and buffer. Receive buffer: ``xbuf[k * ctas + rank]``
+    holds reader k's partial from CTA ``rank``.
+
+    Args:
+        ctas: CTAs per cluster.
+        partials: Partial sums per CTA (readers normalized in the CTA).
+
+    Returns:
+        ``(init, exchange)``. ``init`` runs once the loads are in flight. ``exchange`` maps
+        this CTA's per-reader partial sums to their sums over the cluster, added in rank order
+        so every CTA computes identical bits.
+    """
+
+    def ptx(*lines):
+        """Join ``(instruction, comment)`` pairs into one commented PTX line each."""
+        return "\n".join(f"{code:<64} // {why}" for code, why in lines)
+
+    init = ptx(
+        (".shared .align 8 .b64 xbar;", "barrier: completes when every peer's partials arrive"),
+        (
+            f".shared .align 16 .f32 xbuf[{ctas * partials}];",
+            "receive buffer, one slot per reader/rank",
+        ),
+        ("{", "scope the registers below to this block"),
+        (".reg .pred lead;", "thread 0 sets up the barrier for the whole CTA"),
+        (".reg .u32 tid, mbar;", "thread index; shared address of xbar"),
+        ("mov.u32 tid, %tid.x;", "read this thread's index in the CTA"),
+        ("setp.eq.u32 lead, tid, 0;", "lead = thread 0"),
+        ("mov.u32 mbar, xbar;", "shared-window address of this CTA's barrier"),
+        ("@lead mbarrier.init.shared::cta.b64 [mbar], 1;", "one arrival (the next line) per phase"),
+        (
+            "@lead mbarrier.arrive.expect_tx.shared::cta.b64 _, [mbar], "
+            f"{(ctas - 1) * partials * 4};",
+            "arrive, and expect this many bytes from the peers",
+        ),
+        ("fence.mbarrier_init.release.cluster;", "publish the initialized barrier to peer CTAs"),
+        ("barrier.cluster.arrive.relaxed.aligned;", "signal ready; the wait is in exchange"),
+        ("mov.u32 $0, 0;", "dummy result: inline_asm_elementwise needs an output"),
+        ("}", "end of scope"),
+    )
+    lines = [
+        ("{", "scope the registers below to this block"),
+        (".reg .pred lead, send, own, done;", "thread 0; sends to a peer; own rank; barrier done"),
+        (
+            ".reg .u32 tid, rank, buf, mbar, slot, peer_mbar, peer_slot;",
+            "indices and shared addresses",
+        ),
+        (".reg .f32 v;", "one partial while summing"),
+        ("mov.u32 tid, %tid.x;", "read this thread's index in the CTA"),
+        ("mov.u32 rank, %cluster_ctarank;", "this CTA's rank in the cluster (its column slice)"),
+        ("setp.eq.u32 lead, tid, 0;", "lead = thread 0, the only sender"),
+        ("mov.u32 buf, xbuf;", "shared-window address of the receive buffer"),
+        ("mov.u32 mbar, xbar;", "shared-window address of the barrier"),
+        (
+            "mad.lo.u32 slot, rank, 4, buf;",
+            "&xbuf[rank]: where peers keep this CTA's reader-0 partial",
+        ),
+        ("barrier.cluster.wait.aligned;", "wait until every peer has initialized its barrier"),
+    ]
+    for peer in range(ctas):
+        lines += [
+            (
+                f"setp.ne.and.u32 send, rank, {peer}, lead;",
+                f"send = thread 0 and rank {peer} is a peer",
+            ),
+            (
+                f"@send mapa.shared::cluster.u32 peer_mbar, mbar, {peer};",
+                f"rank {peer}'s barrier address",
+            ),
+            (
+                f"@send mapa.shared::cluster.u32 peer_slot, slot, {peer};",
+                f"rank {peer}'s xbuf[rank]",
+            ),
+        ]
+        for k in range(partials):
+            if k:
+                lines.append(
+                    (
+                        f"@send add.u32 peer_slot, peer_slot, {ctas * 4};",
+                        f"advance to reader {k}'s slots",
+                    )
+                )
+            lines.append(
+                (
+                    "@send st.async.shared::cluster.mbarrier::complete_tx::bytes.b32 "
+                    f"[peer_slot], ${partials + k}, [peer_mbar];",
+                    f"store reader {k}'s partial; count its 4 bytes on rank {peer}'s barrier",
+                )
+            )
+    lines += [
+        ("WAIT_${:uid}:", "retry point (unique label per inlined copy)"),
+        (
+            "mbarrier.try_wait.parity.shared::cta.b64 done, [mbar], 0;",
+            "done once all peers' bytes arrived",
+        ),
+        ("@!done bra WAIT_${:uid};", "not yet: try again"),
+    ]
+    for k in range(partials):
+        for peer in range(ctas):
+            lines += [
+                (
+                    f"setp.eq.u32 own, rank, {peer};",
+                    f"own = rank {peer} is this CTA (its partial is in a register)",
+                ),
+                (f"@own mov.f32 v, ${partials + k};", f"this CTA's reader-{k} partial"),
+                (
+                    f"@!own ld.shared.f32 v, [buf + {(k * ctas + peer) * 4}];",
+                    f"rank {peer}'s reader-{k} partial",
+                ),
+                (
+                    f"add.rn.f32 ${k}, ${k}, v;" if peer else f"mov.f32 ${k}, v;",
+                    "sum in rank order: identical bits in every CTA",
+                ),
+            ]
+    lines.append(("}", "end of scope"))
+    return init, ptx(*lines)
+
+
+# Forward arithmetic and store ownership.
+
+
+@g.jit
+def _load_coefficient(C, INDEX: gl.constexpr):
+    """Return one entry of the coefficient table as a scalar.
+
+    Args:
+        C: Coefficient table from ``_prepare_coefficients``.
+        INDEX: Table index.
+
+    Returns:
+        The coefficient.
+    """
+    indices = gl.full(
+        (1,), INDEX, gl.int32, gl.constexpr(BlockedLayout([1], [32], [gl.num_warps()], [0]))
+    )
+    return gl.sum(C.gather(indices, 0), 0)
+
+
+@g.jit
+def _load_residual(write_tensors, row, stream, cols, GEOMETRY: gl.constexpr, CONFIG: gl.constexpr):
+    """Load one stream's residual fragment (FP32 in 4-wide packets when H allows, or BF16).
+
+    Args:
+        write_tensors: ``_WriteArgs``.
+        row: Row index.
+        stream: Stream index.
+        cols: Column indices of the fragment.
+        GEOMETRY: ``_Geometry``.
+        CONFIG: ``_ForwardConfig``.
+
+    Returns:
+        The residual values, zero outside the row.
+    """
+    H: gl.constexpr = GEOMETRY.H
+    NUM_STREAMS: gl.constexpr = GEOMETRY.STREAMS
+    mask = cols < H
+    residual = write_tensors.residual + row * (NUM_STREAMS * H) + stream * H + cols
+
+    # Explicitly vector-load four contiguous FP32 values with inline PTX when H allows it.
+    if write_tensors.residual.dtype.element_ty != gl.float32:
+        # Stays packed BF16 (two per register) until _mix_fragment widens it at first use.
+        old = gl.load(residual, mask, 0)
+    elif H % 4 == 0:
+        if H % CONFIG.WIDTH:
+            # H and tile widths are multiples of four: each packet is wholly valid or masked.
+            old = gl.inline_asm_elementwise(
+                """
+                { // Begin masked packet-load register scope.
+                    .reg .pred p; // Declare the packet validity predicate.
+                    setp.ne.u32 p, $8, 0; // Check whether the four-value packet is valid.
+                    mov.b32 $0, 0; // Zero the first value for a masked packet.
+                    mov.b32 $1, 0; // Zero the second value for a masked packet.
+                    mov.b32 $2, 0; // Zero the third value for a masked packet.
+                    mov.b32 $3, 0; // Zero the fourth value for a masked packet.
+                    @p ld.global.nc.v4.f32 {$0,$1,$2,$3},[$4]; // Load four valid FP32 values.
+                } // End masked packet-load register scope.
+                """,
+                "=f,=f,=f,=f,l,l,l,l,r,r,r,r",
+                (residual.to(gl.uint64), mask.to(gl.int32)),
+                dtype=gl.float32,
+                is_pure=False,
+                pack=4,
+            )
+        else:
+            old = gl.inline_asm_elementwise(
+                """
+                { // Begin packet-load scope.
+                    ld.global.nc.v4.f32 {$0,$1,$2,$3},[$4]; // Load four contiguous FP32 values.
+                } // End packet-load scope.
+                """,
+                "=f,=f,=f,=f,l,l,l,l",
+                (residual.to(gl.uint64),),
+                dtype=gl.float32,
+                is_pure=False,
+                pack=4,
+            )
+    else:
+        old = gl.load(residual, mask, 0)
+    return old
+
+
+@g.jit
+def _load_fragment(write_tensors, row, cols, GEOMETRY: gl.constexpr, CONFIG: gl.constexpr):
+    """Issue one fragment's update loads, plus every stream's residual load with LOADS_FIRST.
+
+    Args:
+        write_tensors: ``_WriteArgs``.
+        row: Row index.
+        cols: Column indices of the fragment.
+        GEOMETRY: ``_Geometry``.
+        CONFIG: ``_ForwardConfig``.
+
+    Returns:
+        ``(update, other, olds)``: the BF16 updates (``other`` repeats ``update`` without a
+        shortcut add) and, with LOADS_FIRST, each stream's residual values (else an empty
+        tuple).
+    """
+    H: gl.constexpr = GEOMETRY.H
+    mask = cols < H
+    update = gl.load(write_tensors.update + (row * H + cols), mask, 0)
+    other = update  # unused without a shortcut add
+    if write_tensors.other_update is not None:
+        other = gl.load(write_tensors.other_update + (row * H + cols), mask, 0)
+    NUM_STREAMS: gl.constexpr = GEOMETRY.STREAMS
+    olds = ()
+    if CONFIG.LOADS_FIRST:
+        for stream in gl.static_range(NUM_STREAMS):
+            olds += (_load_residual(write_tensors, row, stream, cols, GEOMETRY, CONFIG),)
+    return update, other, olds
+
+
+@g.jit
+def _mix_fragment(
+    write_tensors,
+    coefficients,
+    row,
+    cols,
+    GEOMETRY: gl.constexpr,
+    TWO_READERS: gl.constexpr,
+    CONFIG: gl.constexpr,
+    OWNER,
+    LOADED=None,
+):
+    """Write one fragment's residual streams and return its folded reader inputs.
+
+    Preserves the native writer's FMA/RN contraction pattern, which checkpoint replay
+    reproduces bit for bit.
+
+    Args:
+        write_tensors: ``_WriteArgs``.
+        coefficients: Coefficient table from ``_prepare_coefficients``.
+        row: Row index.
+        cols: Column indices of the fragment.
+        GEOMETRY: ``_Geometry``.
+        TWO_READERS: Whether there is a second reader.
+        CONFIG: ``_ForwardConfig``.
+        OWNER: Mask of the columns this CTA stores.
+        LOADED: Loads already issued by ``_load_fragment``, or None to load here.
+
+    Returns:
+        The two readers' pre-norm inputs (the second is zero with one reader), zero outside the row.
+    """
+    H: gl.constexpr = GEOMETRY.H
+    NUM_STREAMS: gl.constexpr = GEOMETRY.STREAMS
+    HAS_RETENTION: gl.constexpr = GEOMETRY.HAS_RETENTION
+    mask = cols < H
+    if LOADED is None:
+        LOADED = _load_fragment(write_tensors, row, cols, GEOMETRY, CONFIG)
+    update, other, olds = LOADED
+    update = update.to(gl.float32)
+    if write_tensors.other_update is not None:  # shortcut add
+        other = other.to(gl.float32)
+        update = (update + other).to(gl.bfloat16).to(gl.float32)
+        if write_tensors.summed_update is not None:
+            gl.store(write_tensors.summed_update + row * H + cols, update, mask)
+    x0 = gl.full(mask.shape, 0, gl.float32, mask.type.layout)
+    x1 = gl.full(mask.shape, 0, gl.float32, mask.type.layout)
+    update_mix0 = 0.0
+    update_mix1 = 0.0
+    for stream in gl.static_range(NUM_STREAMS):
+        owner = OWNER & (not CONFIG.SPLIT or gl.program_id(1) == (stream == NUM_STREAMS - 1))
+        if CONFIG.LOADS_FIRST:
+            old = olds[stream]
+        else:
+            old = _load_residual(write_tensors, row, stream, cols, GEOMETRY, CONFIG)
+        old = old.to(gl.float32)  # exact for BF16; a no-op for FP32
+
+        write = _load_coefficient(coefficients, stream)
+        retain = _load_coefficient(coefficients, NUM_STREAMS + stream) if HAS_RETENTION else 1.0
+
+        separate = write * update + retain * old
+        # Preserve the native writer's row/stream contraction pattern;
+        # checkpoint replay uses exactly these RN/FMA boundaries.
+        contracted = (stream == 0) | ((stream == 1) & (row % 32 < 12))
+        value = gl.where(contracted, gl.fma(write, update, retain * old), separate)
+
+        stored = value.to(write_tensors.output.dtype.element_ty)  # RN for a BF16 residual
+        if not CONFIG.STORE_LATE:
+            gl.store(
+                write_tensors.output + row * (NUM_STREAMS * H) + stream * H + cols,
+                stored,
+                mask & owner,
+            )
+        beta0 = _load_coefficient(coefficients, 2 * NUM_STREAMS + stream)
+        x0 = gl.fma(beta0 * retain, old, x0)
+        update_mix0 = gl.fma(beta0, write, update_mix0)
+        if TWO_READERS:
+            beta1 = _load_coefficient(coefficients, 3 * NUM_STREAMS + stream)
+            x1 = gl.fma(beta1 * retain, old, x1)
+            update_mix1 = gl.fma(beta1, write, update_mix1)
+        if CONFIG.STORE_LATE:
+            gl.store(
+                write_tensors.output + row * (NUM_STREAMS * H) + stream * H + cols,
+                stored,
+                mask & owner,
+            )
+    x0 = gl.fma(update_mix0, update, x0)
+    if TWO_READERS:
+        x1 = gl.fma(update_mix1, update, x1)
+    return gl.where(mask, x0, 0.0), gl.where(mask, x1, 0.0)
+
+

+def reduce_jobs(jobs):
+    """Pack reductions directly into disjoint CTA ranges, without equal-shape grouping."""
+    packed, grid = [], 0
+    for job in jobs:
+        source, output, axis, tile, chunk, factor = job[:6]
+        combo = job[6] if len(job) == 7 else None
+        width, height = source.shape[1 - axis], source.shape[axis]
+        chunk = chunk or triton.next_power_of_2(height)
+        size = output.numel() if output.ndim == 1 else width
+        end = grid + triton.cdiv(width, tile) * triton.cdiv(height, chunk)

+@g.jit
+def _fma2(a, b, c):
+    # Two independent RN FP32 FMAs (a * b + c), issued as one packed f32x2 instruction.
+    return gl.inline_asm_elementwise(
+        """
+        { // Begin paired-FMA register scope.
+            .reg .b64 a,b,c,r; // Declare packed FP32 operand and result registers.
+            mov.b64 a,{$2,$3}; // Pack the first pair of multiplicands.
+            mov.b64 b,{$4,$5}; // Pack the second pair of multiplicands.
+            mov.b64 c,{$6,$7}; // Pack the two addends.
+            fma.rn.f32x2 r,a,b,c; // Compute two round-to-nearest fused multiply-adds.
+            mov.b64 {$0,$1},r; // Unpack the two FP32 results.

+        "=f,=f,f,f,f,f,f,f",
+        [a, b, c],
+        dtype=gl.float32,
+        is_pure=True,
+        pack=2,
+    )

+
+def _descriptor(tensor, tile_shape):
+    if tensor is None:
+        return None
+    bits = tensor.element_size() * 8
+    layout = NVMMASharedLayout(swizzle_byte_width=bits * 4, element_bitwidth=bits, rank=2)
+    return TensorDescriptor.from_tensor(tensor, list(tile_shape), layout)
+
+
+@g.jit
+def _mul_rn(a, b):
+    # Uncontracted IEEE multiply; libdevice.mul_rn flushes subnormals under reflect-FTZ.
+    return gl.inline_asm_elementwise(

+    return gl.inline_asm_elementwise(
+        "add.rn.f32 $0,$1,$2;", "=f,f,f", [a, b], dtype=gl.float32, is_pure=True, pack=1
+    )
+
+
+@g.jit
+def _forward_value(previous, update, write, retain, rows, stream):
+    """Match forward's explicit fused/separate FP32 contraction boundaries."""
+    retained = _mul_rn(retain, previous)
+    separate = _add_rn(_mul_rn(write, update), retained)
+    contracted = (stream == 0) | ((stream == 1) & (rows % 32 < 12))
+    return gl.where(contracted, gl.fma(write, update, retained), separate)

+
+An exclusive TELinear consumer defers its wgrad GEMM until the shortcut
+backward hands off the prepared columnwise operand. An extra weight dependency holds its
+AccumulateGrad until that GEMM finishes. TE still owns both GEMMs, quantization
+of weights/dy, gradient accumulation, and distributed-weight finalization.

+state or global TE function is replaced.

+def reader_for(tensor):
+    """Find a producer through views/detaches without retaining its FP8 allocation."""
+    data = getattr(tensor, "_rowwise_data", None)
+    if data is None:
+        return None
+    return _READERS.get(StorageWeakRef(data.untyped_storage()))

+class Reader:
+    """Detached reconstruction state owned by one autograd boundary."""
+
+    def __init__(self, tensor, saved, consumer=None):
+        self.shape, self.device = tuple(saved.update.shape), saved.update.device
+        self.consumer = None if consumer is None else ref(consumer)
+        self.pending = []
+        storage = tensor._rowwise_data.untyped_storage()
+        # Holding only the intrusive weak reference prevents StorageImpl address
+        # reuse from aliasing this registry entry, without retaining GPU bytes.
+        _READERS[StorageWeakRef(storage)] = self
+        tensor._shortcut_mxfp8_reader = self
+
+    def empty_columnwise(self, shape):
+        """Allocate this reader's column operand with the consumer view shape."""
+        from .kernel_utils import allocate_operand
+
+        return allocate_operand(self.shape, self.device, columnwise=True).view(shape)
+
+    def compute_wgrad(self, previous, column):
+        """Submit delayed GEMMs as soon as the boundary's column operand is ready."""
+        if self.pending and column is None:
+            raise RuntimeError("deferred shortcut weight gradients require fused MXFP8 columns")
+        stream = torch.cuda.current_stream(previous.device)
+        for tensors, function, weight, consumer_stream in self.pending:
+            tensors[0]._columnwise_data = column._columnwise_data
+            tensors[0]._columnwise_scale_inv = column._columnwise_scale_inv
+
+            # TE's dy and wgrad buffers belong to its backward stream. Keep
+            # their allocation lifetimes there, and order the new column
+            # input and boundary completion through explicit stream waits.
+            if consumer_stream != stream:
+                consumer_stream.wait_stream(stream)
+            with torch.cuda.stream(consumer_stream):
+                column._columnwise_data.record_stream(consumer_stream)
+                column._columnwise_scale_inv.record_stream(consumer_stream)
+                dw, _ = function(*tensors)
+                if weight is not None:
+                    from transformer_engine.pytorch.distributed_weight import finalize_weight_grads

+        stream = torch.cuda.current_stream(previous.device)
+        for _, _, _, consumer_stream in self.pending:
+            if consumer_stream != stream:
+                stream.wait_stream(consumer_stream)
+        # Keep TE buffers alive until both streams have submitted their work.
+        self.pending.clear()

+    individual activation save slot after forward instead.
